newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Dutch banks interested in Bosnia private corp.
newsitem.headline: Dutch banks interested in Bosnia private corp.

text.p: Two Dutch banks are considering buying equity in a private finance corporation set up by the World Bank to channel foreign funds and extend loans to local companies, a World Bank official said on Thursday.
"ABN AMRO and ING from the Netherlands expressed interest," Saumya Mitra, the World Bank's deputy mission director, told reporters on Thursday.
The World Bank said this month it planned to launch the corporation with some 50 million German marks ($30 million) collected from repayments of credit lines in the country's Moslem-Croat federation.
The Dutch banks, known for their keen interest in emerging markets, were still gathering information about the project, Mitra said, adding that other banks were interested in the corporation as well.

The private loan corporation, which would be run privately by foreign and local banks, is meant to provide a boost to a post-war economic recovery and to lay the foundation for a market-oriented banking system.
The presence of foreign banks will also help restore faith in a financial system which was devastated when old Yugoslavia collapsed into war six years ago, Mitra said.

"The entry of a top-name foreign bank would send a very powerful signal about political and economic stability in Bosnia but more important, I think it will create among the local population a greater confidence in the banking system," he said.
Bosnians lost an estimated four billion German marks when Yugoslav banks froze foreign currency savings in 1991.
